existing_interactions.hypothesis: First-half totals depend on first-half pace, which differs from game pace and is team-specific.
A starter's early fouls create the biggest first-half-specific variance.
Half total, half spread and game lines must be coherent; inconsistent half prices are the main edge.
Late-half bonus FT scoring increases first-half totals for teams with good FT shooters.

first_half.existing_mechanism: First-half scoring is driven by starters and tempo, the first-half share of game scoring (team-specific), early foul trouble, and half-end bonus dynamics. Game-level markets are better priced than half-level derivatives, so inconsistencies between half and game lines are a source of edge; ties in half winners matter.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Title odds are convex in rating and sensitive to single-game variance; high-variance teams are mispriced when ratings alone are used.
Pre-bracket futures integrate over seed/region assignment, which resolves at Selection Sunday.
A single star injury changes title odds by large factors; mixture models matter.
Brand teams may be overpriced vs the book consensus; test the gap by popularity.

futures_champion.existing_mechanism: Title probability = product of advancement probabilities through a 6-round single-elimination bracket, with team strength uncertain and single-game variance high. Before Selection Sunday it integrates over seed and region uncertainty; afterward it follows the actual path. Star injury risk and path matchups dominate the tails; markets include brand bias and long-shot bias.

team_total.existing_mechanism: Team points = own possessions x own efficiency against the opponent's defense, correlated with margin: favorites' bench minutes in blowouts and underdogs' late free throws shape the team distribution.
